summary: Joshua T. Katz is a linguist who studied at Yale, Oxford, and Harvard. He served as Cotsen Professor in the Humanities at Princeton University (1998–2022) and became a Senior Fellow at the American Enterprise Institute around 2022.
Josiah Dwight Whitney studied at Yale University (~1835–1839). He was affiliated with the University of Iowa (~1855–1858) and served as a professor at Harvard University from 1865 to 1896.

Josiah Royce was a philosopher who studied at the University of California, Berkeley, the University of Göttingen under Hermann Lotze, and Johns Hopkins University. He taught at Berkeley (~1878–1882) and was a faculty member at Harvard University (1882–1916).

José Ignacio Cabezón studied at Caltech, Sera Monastery, and the University of Wisconsin–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa. He served at the Iliff School of Theology (~1989–2001) and became Dalai Lama Professor at UC Santa Barbara in 2001.
Jotika Khur-Yearn is a scholar in Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of Kate Crosby (attested 2012).

Jowita Kramer is an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen and David P. Jackson, and Munich under Jens-Uwe Hartmann. She held posts at Munich and became professor at Leipzig University in 2021.

Joy Cecile Brennan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago, where she studied under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, and Constance Furey, and studied under traditional teacher Diane Martin.
Juan Wu works in Buddhist studies and Indology, earning a PhD from Cardiff University under the doctoral supervision of Max Deeg (attested 2012).

Judit Törzsök is an Indologist who studied at Eötvös Loránd University and Merton College, Oxford under Alexis Sanderson. She served as associate professor at Lille 3 University (from 2001) and became a professor at EPHE in 2018.

Judith Simmer-Brown, a Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Cornell College, Florida State, Columbia, and Walden University, as well as under Chögyam Trungpa. She was appointed Distinguished Professor Emerita at Naropa University, where she began in 1977.

Juhn Y. Ahn is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He earned his PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007 and was an associate professor at the University of Michigan (attested 2019).
Juhyung Rhi is a scholar of Buddhist studies and art history. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, and became a professor of art history at Seoul National University in 1992.
Juichiro Tanabe is a scholar in philosophy who studied at the University of Bradford (2000–2001, PhD candidate attested 2010) and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire was a French scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Lycée Louis-le-Grand and Bourbon college, he served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

Jules Bloch studied at EPHE, INALCO, and the University of Paris under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet. He held posts at EPHE, INALCO, and the Collège de France, where he was Chair of Sanskrit from 1936 to 1951.

Jules Brooks Levinson is a Tibetan and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under Jeffrey Hopkins. He served as an assistant professor of religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Jules Michelet was a French historian who studied at Lycée Charlemagne. He taught at the École Normale Supérieure, served as section chief at the Archives nationales (1831–1851), and was Professor of History at the Collège de France (1838–1852).

Jules Mohl studied at Tübingen and under Silvestre de Sacy, Abel-Rémusat, and Eugène Burnouf. He taught oriental literature at the University of Tübingen (1826–1834) and served as Professor of Persian at the Collège de France (1847–1876).

Jules Oppert was an Assyriologist and linguist who earned his PhD at Kiel University. He was a professor at the École des langues orientales (from 1857) and later served as professor at the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Julia A. B. Hegewald is an Indologist and architectural historian who studied at SOAS University of London, Oxford, and RWTH Aachen University. In 2010, she became a professor at the University of Bonn.
